chapter: Dance tastes, big bands and the boat
title: Arguing with Captain Streckfus over music on the steamer
summary: DeDroit tells how he refused to change his New Orleans style for Captain Streckfus on the boat and left, and mentions his $500-a-night fee and Dutch Andrews.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Talking about style, on your other interview you mentioned arguing with the Captain Strykfuss about the kind of music you'd play on the boat. He said something about he wanted you to play like what he'd heard in St. Louis, and he says you're in New Orleans and you play like what people in New Orleans wanted. How would you contrast the two? What would be the…

I didn't contrast them because I didn't know what they played in St. Louis. But to give me a list of ten best tunes in St. Louis that some of them I'd never heard of, but didn't know how they played out. I just said, Captain, I play New Orleans music. And I don't think that the people in New Orleans want to sing most music. I said, I don't know what it is. And then he said to me, he said, well you're working against me. I said, Captain, I'm not working against you. I said, with all due respect to you, you're a fine man, but you're never going to be bothered with me again because I'm never going to play on this boat again. Well what year was that? Oh, I retired in the 50s. Now I would say it was in the 50s. I see. I see. And he said to me, you play good, honest music. I said, I know what you have to do. I wouldn't give him a thing because he was a Martin man. You see when he pulled out from the wharf and you were in prison, he misbehaved and put you in a brig. And he wanted to be everything. I said, Captain, why don't you let me run the boat? You run the band and we'll both wind up on the wharf. Well I'll tell you what to play and how to play. But the trouble was it was the other musicians. They say, Johnny Dwight only plays for you in Lent. They said to me, you want to play for me in Lent? I said, Captain, I play for you and I can play for you. Do you want me in Lent? If you don't, I'll go play somewhere else. He couldn't understand that. Because he had people who played well but were not like Dutch Andrews, who I think is a fine trumpet player. Dutch can't read. I tried to use him and he couldn't read. But he has a big tone and he plays nice and if he'd only had sense enough to make some of the other fellas play a little soft and let Dutch do a little playing, you'd really hear something because his licks clean, he plays nice. That's it. They would, he would take advice from people who didn't know anything about music. See? And then he's always fun with the microphone. And I'd go up and get a cup of coffee. I know what I'm going to do and I'd give to Dom B and I know how my band's going to play or else they're going to hear from me. You know what I mean? And I'm not going to change my style of playing on the boat doing like, I'm playing for the country club, I'm going to play for the same of them. Because I got the engagements because I played the style that they liked. See? And I must have had something. People don't put out a lot of music, pay over. I made it. I shouldn't say that I made it. I was $500 a night just for myself. If somebody likes you and they had the money, charge them. That's all. That's $500 for you? For me, yeah. Not the band? No, no. I used to, Mr. Cobb used to let me off when I'd go up to Greenwood and play for the society people. Give you all kinds of money. Greenwood, Mississippi? Yeah, and the Delta. Other places. You
